title: Both numbers have five digits. Which one is greater?
description: Harpreet's family stores wheat in two godowns. The video lines up the two weights on the place value chart and compares them from the left.
teaching_notes: One idea: with equal digits, compare place by place from the left and stop where the digits first differ. Watch for children who look at the last digit.

video_script.why: The child knows that more digits is greater but must now compare two numbers with the same number of digits.
video_script.substitution: Line the digits up in columns and compare from the biggest place on the left; the first place where they differ decides.
video_script.anchor: wheat stored in two godowns of Harpreet's family, weighed in kilograms
video_script.wrong_answer: fifty six thousand two hundred ninety eight is greater
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu looks at the last digit, eight and one, and picks the number that ends in eight. The ones place is the smallest place.
video_script.payoff_line: fifty six thousand three hundred twenty one is greater

final_answer.value: 56,321 is greater than 56,298, because the hundreds digit 3 is greater than 2
final_answer.spoken: fifty six thousand three hundred twenty one is greater than fifty six thousand two hundred ninety eight, because the hundreds digit three is greater than two

never_show: the your-turn answer: 47,650 is greater than 47,609
maths_rules: ten thousands: 5 and 5, equal; thousands: 6 and 6, equal; hundreds: 3 and 2, different
slip: 8 > 1 in the ones place, but the ones place is the smallest place
your turn: 47,650 and 47,609; 4, 7, 6 equal; tens 5 and 0; 5 > 0 so 47,650 is greater; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: compare from the left and stop at the first difference. Wrong idea: compare from the right. The two numbers sit one under the other on the place value chart.
